definitions.explanation: A traditional Japanese room with tatami mat flooring, typically featuring fusuma (sliding doors) and a tokonoma (alcove).

notes:
{和室|わしつ} is composed of {和|わ} (Japanese) + ⟦{室|しつ}→室：09946_shitsu⟧ (room). It refers to a traditional Japanese-style room with ⟦{畳|たたみ}→畳：02224_tatami⟧ (tatami mat) flooring.

TYPICAL FEATURES:
- ⟦{畳|たたみ}→畳：02224_tatami⟧: tatami mats (straw flooring)
- ⟦{襖|ふすま}→襖：03908_fusuma⟧: sliding paper doors (between rooms)
- ⟦{障子|しょうじ}→障子：04201_shouji⟧: paper sliding screens (for windows)
- ⟦{床|とこ}の{間|ま}→床の間：05797_tokonoma⟧: decorative alcove
- {押|お}し{入|い}れ: built-in closet for ⟦{布団|ふとん}→布団：01720_futon⟧

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {和室|わしつ}: Japanese-style room (tatami, futon, floor seating)
- ⟦{洋室|ようしつ}→洋室：15741_youshitsu⟧: Western-style room (flooring, beds, chairs)

USAGE:
Common when describing ⟦{旅館|りょかん}→旅館：01049_ryokan⟧ (Japanese inns), apartments, or house layouts. Room size is measured in {畳|じょう} (tatami mats): {六畳|ろくじょう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{和室|わしつ} (a 6-tatami Japanese room). Modern Japanese homes often have one {和室|わしつ} alongside ⟦{洋室|ようしつ}→洋室：15741_youshitsu⟧.
